paper.title: SteP: Stacked LLM Policies for Web Actions
paper.central_claim: Dynamically compose human-defined prompted policies through a stack that adapts control depth to task complexity, improving diverse web-task success over flat/prior policies while using less context, demonstration data and overall cost/inference time.

signatures.object: Single long-context web policy replaced by stack of callable prompted policies
signatures.information: Partial DOM/elementIDs, objective, URL, frame-local observation/reason/action history, child return. Browser state persists across calls. No future observations or outcome oracle.
signatures.operation: Initialize root if stack empty; top policy emits environment action (returned to env.step), invocation (initialize/push empty-history child) or stop (pop, append return to parent). Internal call/return does not step browser.
signatures.output: Browser primitive or eventual root termination; variable-depth recursive composition
signatures.conditions: Compatible manually designed library, sufficient arguments/return information, capable instruction-following model. No independent subtask-success validator or finite-recursion guarantee.
signatures.feedback: Browser observation and self-declared child response; benchmark outcomes evaluate but do not select persistent updates.
signatures.selection_rule/data: LLM chooses subroutine/action at runtime; human writes prompts from recurrent subtasks. No autonomous policy acceptance/rejection.
signatures.persistence: Fixed library across tasks; stack and histories are episodic; backbone unchanged.
signatures.later_use: Reuse existing human-authored policy definitions on later tasks/subtasks, not discovery of retained skills.
signatures.claimed_effect: Reduce irrelevant prompt interference and handle flexible-depth tasks.
signatures.failure_boundary: Missing child information can create endless loop; popping context does not undo browser state.

signatures.object: Policy-specific conditional examples and scoped prompt capacity
signatures.information: Dedicated instructions/few-shot pairs; DOM serialized into IDs/text; note stores within-task content in previous actions.
signatures.operation: Only active policy prompt/context is shown rather than concatenating full library. MiniWoB examples disambiguate UI controls; Flat4K/8K concatenates library.
signatures.conditions: Per-policy context generally <4K; example bodies are not included in fixed paper.
signatures.feedback: Static demonstrations and author benchmark measurements, not experience retention.
signatures.selection_rule/data: 10MiniWoB demonstrations from6tasks; main24state-action pairs versus later21maximum examples; Flat7examples. Development/test separation incompletely auditable.
signatures.later_use: Compose subroutines on other tasks; live-site evidence is reference comparison.
signatures.claimed_effect: Improved success and fewer input tokens per successful WebArena trajectory.
signatures.failure_boundary: Total demo capacity, extra model calls and successful-only token selection confound pure hierarchy/cost effects.

gap.author_gap: One giant prompt mixes behaviors and long histories; fixed shallow hierarchies cannot adapt to nested recurrent subroutines.
gap.checked_gap: Dynamic callable policies and scoped history address a real interference/control bottleneck. Content-enriched Flat controls show residue beyond adding instructions, but do not isolate stack, example capacity, tuning and call budgets.

E.causality.reason: Same-family Flat4K/8K/library and zero/few controls useful, but stack/history/prompt engineering/extra calls/total example capacity not separately isolated; prior GPT versions differ.

E.holdout.reason: Composition beyond six demo tasks and cross-site comparison give limited breadth; examples and development/test separation cannot be audited. Primary online tests remain constructed web-family settings; no outcome-checked independent transfer.

E.statistics.reason: 50seeds/task,20CRMscenarios and taskwise failures are substantive denominators. No WebArena repeat spread/CI; n=3API is not independent repetition,24/21count ambiguity remains.

E.cost.reason: Context caps/actions/successful-only input means useful, but SteP uses more WebArena browser actions and all-attempt output/API cost/wall-clock not measured; broad overall-cost claim unsupported.
